title: A simple method for the synthesis of biochar nanodots using hydrothermal reactor
author: Guo, Bao, et al.
materials: Biochars of interest from a wide range of feedstock, pyrolysis temperatures, gas-phase components, and activation chemistries. In this description both of the feedstock for the biochars used were soybean straw and cattle manure. The two agricultural-biomass were collected from a farm in the city of Clinton, Mississippi, US. After air-dried, crushed, pulverized and sieved through a 10-mesh sieve, subsamples of both materials were then respectively pyrolyzed in a tube furnace (Thermo Scientific Lindberg/Blue M mini-mite tube furnaces). The pyrolysis temperature was set as 500 °C. The pyrolysis atmosphere was nitrogen and gas flow rate was 5 mL/min. The heating rate was set as 5 °C/min and the residence time was 2 h. After natural cooling, the bulk-biochar product was thus obtained.

steps.title: Prepare bulk biochar via pyrolysis
steps.instruction: Air‑dry, crush, pulverize soybean straw and cattle manure, sieve through a 10‑mesh screen, then pyrolyze each subsample in a Thermo Scientific Lindberg/Blue M mini‑mite tube furnace under nitrogen at 500 °C (heating rate 5 °C/min, gas flow 5 mL/min) for 2 h; allow natural cooling to obtain bulk biochar.

steps.title: Grind bulk biochar
steps.instruction: Grind the obtained bulk biochar in a commercial blender.

steps.title: Sieve ground biochar
steps.instruction: Pass the ground biochar through a 60‑mesh sieve to obtain a homogenized fraction smaller than 60 mesh.

steps.title: Acid digestion in hydrothermal reactor
steps.instruction: Place 1 g of the <60‑mesh biochar into a hydrothermal reactor, add 15 mL concentrated HNO₃ and 45 mL concentrated H₂SO₄ (per gram of biochar), and let the mixture stand statically at room temperature for 2 h in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Static reaction 2 h at room temperature

steps.title: Dilute and rest
steps.instruction: Transfer the reaction mixture to a beaker containing 1000 mL deionized water, stir with a glass rod for 1 min, then let stand for 10 min.

steps.title: Separate solids by vacuum filtration
steps.instruction: Remove the solid portion and filter the suspension using a vacuum filter equipped with a 0.22‑µm membrane.

steps.title: Dry nanodot‑covered membrane
steps.instruction: Place the filter membrane bearing the biochar nanodots in an oven at 65 °C for 48 h to dry.
